items.q: Can a foreigner buy property in Dubai?
items.a: Yes. Since 2002, foreigners can buy property as full freehold ownership in designated zones — that's 90% of all new construction in Dubai, including Marina, Downtown, Palm Jumeirah, Creek Harbour, Business Bay.

items.q: What is the minimum budget to enter the market?
items.a: From $145,000 — studios and compact apartments in Dubailand and JVC. Investor resident visa starts at $205,000 (ready property) + $545,000 owned; Golden Visa — from $2,180,000.

items.q: What taxes does an investor pay in the UAE?
items.a: 0% personal income tax, 0% rental income tax, 0% capital gains tax. One-time DLD fee on purchase — 4% of value. Annual service charge depends on the property (10–25 AED/sq.ft).

items.q: How do I get a Golden Visa through property?
items.a: The 10-year Golden Visa is granted on property purchase from 2,000,000 AED (~$545,000) owned. A 2-year visa — from 750,000 AED investment. The visa covers spouse, children and parents. No mandatory residence required.

items.q: What is off-plan and what are the benefits?
items.a: Off-plan is buying during construction with 40/60 or 60/40 interest-free payment plans. Benefits: price 20–35% below ready, capital growth of 25–40% until handover, exclusive layouts. Risk minimised: RERA escrow accounts protect buyer payments.

items.q: How do developer payment plans work?
items.a: Standard 40/60: 40% during construction in equal tranches (5–10% every 6 months), 60% on handover. You can take a UAE bank mortgage at 4–6% per year for the final payment. No foreign credit history check.

items.q: Can a non-resident get a mortgage?
items.a: Yes. UAE banks (Mashreq, Emirates NBD, FAB) issue mortgages to non-residents up to 50% of property value, rate 4.5–6.5%, term up to 25 years. Income proof required (from any country) from $5,000/month.

items.q: What is the real ROI and cash flow?
items.a: Average ROI in Dubai in 2025 — 7.2%. Leaders: JVC and Dubailand 10–12%, Marina 8.4%, Downtown 7.2%, Palm 6.8%. Occupancy average 87–94%. On top of ROI there's annual capital growth of 5–7% (the 2024 market showed +18%).

items.q: What if the developer fails to complete?
items.a: All buyer payments go to a RERA escrow account — the developer has no access to them until each construction stage is completed. If deadlines slip by more than 12 months, the investor is entitled to a full refund + penalty. ShanGroup works only with Tier-1 developers (EMAAR, DAMAC, SOBHA, NAKHEEL, MERAAS).

items.q: How does a remote deal work?
items.a: Documents can be signed remotely via notarised power of attorney. Settlement — bank transfer to escrow. DLD registration takes 1 business day. ShanGroup fully assists: account opening, lawyer selection, tax consultation, key handover.
